🇲🇽💧 <u>SHEINBAUM AND DELFINA FLOOD-PROOF THE EAST OF EDOMEX</u>

Plan Oriente is rehabilitating the Churubusco-Xochiaca tunnel: 16,000 liters per second of drainage capacity shielding over a million residents of Nezahualcóyotl, Chimalhuacán and La Paz. Generations of floods in the Valley of Mexico's east, answered with hydraulic works at scale — not promises.

🇲🇽🌲 <u>PROFEPA SEIZES 3,008 M³ OF ILLEGAL TIMBER, SHUTTERS 27 SITES</u>

Mexico's environmental prosecutor ran its third simultaneous forest crackdown across 26 states: 3,008 cubic meters of timber seized and 27 sites closed — including illegal logging inside the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve in Michoacán, where pine, oak and white cedar were felled. 55 inspections, 28 transport checkpoints, 82 pieces of sawmill machinery confiscated. Enforcement with teeth.

🇲🇽🕊️ <u>"WE'RE NOT LEAVING LA MONTAÑA": THE STATE STAYS IN GUERRERO</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez presented the Master Plan for Montaña Alta y Baja: since May 13, nineteen federal agencies on the ground in 19 communities across Atlixtac, Chilapa, Olinalá and Zapotitlán Tablas — security plus health, education, housing and field support across 13 axes. "No nos vamos a salir de la región." Not an operation, a presence.

🇲🇽🏺 <u>BOSTON HANDS BACK 1,132 PRE-HISPANIC PIECES TO MEXICO</u>

Mexico recovered 1,132 archaeological pieces voluntarily restituted at its consulate in Boston: 1,053 ceramic sherds, 36 shark teeth, obsidian and flint blades, figurines from the southeast. Coordinated by SRE, Culture and INAH. Under the 4T, more than 17,000 looted artifacts have been brought home — quiet diplomacy, piece by piece.

🇲🇽📱 <u>MEXICO CONSULTS 1 MILLION TEACHERS BEFORE REGULATING PHONES IN SCHOOLS</u>

No decree from above: Mexico's SEP will ask over a million teachers in 200,000+ schools what they think about cellphone use in classrooms, during the technical councils on August 24-25. "We're going to ask the teachers first what their opinion is," Sheinbaum said — 16 states already regulate it, and the goal is a national rule built with the schools, not against them.

🇲🇽🎓 Sheinbaum doubled the goal: 400,000 new high school places so no teenager is left out. "We will have 400,000 new places, because the best place for teenagers to be is in school. The President doubled the goal — we had planned 200,000 places, and she told us we must make it 400,000." — Tania Rodríguez, Undersecretary of Upper Secondary Education In 2025, 88 schools were built or expanded (44,000 places). In 2026: 485 more schools, 156,240 places, over 10 billion pesos. Enrollment for the new Bachillerato Nacional "Margarita Maza" is open.

🇲🇽⚖️ A US court ruled Meta legally responsible for the harm its platform design causes children — and ordered the design changed. "The problem is not bad users posting negative content; it is a system designed to foster overuse, unwanted contact, and exposure to unwanted, harmful content." — Dr. Ravi Iyer, USC Neely Center, on the New Mexico v. Meta ruling The New Mexico ruling is the first to force a platform to modify design decisions: age verification, hidden like counts for minors, no push notifications at night or school hours, usage time caps, and private-by-default teen accounts — for 5 years.

🇲🇽📱 Meta's own internal research: 13% of Instagram users aged 13-15 received unwanted sexual advances in a single week. "Meta's own internal research revealed that 13% of Instagram users between 13 and 15 years old had received some unwanted sexual advance in the last 7 days." — Dr. Ravi Iyer, former Meta data-science research lead, at Mexico's morning press conference The figure comes from Meta's internal research made public in the New Mexico v. Meta litigation. A related internal survey found 19.2% of children 13-15 saw unwanted nudity or sexual content in one week. Iyer, now at USC's Neely Center, spent 4.5 years at Meta designing social networks.
